features.name: Structural token contract complete for every look
features.acceptance: When a unit test enumerates every entry of the exported LOOKS record, then every look object exposes all 21 required structural token keys with non-null values.
features.notes: 21 keys = typography 7 + spacing 7 + radius 2 + surface 1 + motion 4. The existing __tests__/stores/themeStore.test.ts asserts every token value matches a hex/rgba regex, which numeric structural tokens will violate — that suite needs new describe blocks, not a patched regex.

oracle.condition: Import LOOKS from src/theme/looks.ts and iterate Object.entries(LOOKS). For each look, read the key set of its typography, spacing, radius, surface and motion groups.
oracle.assertion: For each of the 2 looks, the flattened key set deep-equals the exported REQUIRED_STRUCTURAL_KEYS array of length 21, and every resolved value is neither null nor undefined.
oracle.failure_mode: A look is missing a key (length < 21), carries an extra undeclared key, or resolves a key to null or undefined — any of which crashes a screen that reads that token at render time.

features.name: Zero hardcoded style literals outside documented exceptions
features.acceptance: When a unit test scans app/** and src/components/** excluding the three files documented as deliberately hardcoded, then the scan reports zero numeric style literals.
features.notes: impl_file is deliberately null: the implementation is the ABSENCE of literals across 33 files, not a single module, so there is no file that can carry CHALLENGER sentinels. TWO BASELINE NUMBERS, both real, different scopes — the spec cites 901 from the 2026-09-09 audit, which counted app/_layout.tsx, UpdateCheckScreen.tsx and margin/elevation props now out of scope; this test's own first run under its exact exclusion rules located 767. The oracle's ASSERTION is length 0, which both satisfy; 901 is historical context, not a threshold. Recorded here so a later reader does not mistake the discrepancy for fraud. Exclusions: app/_layout.tsx and src/components/UpdateCheckScreen.tsx pin brand navy to match the native splash; app/radar.tsx Mapbox-native props are not React Native styles. 15 of 33 files use module-scope StyleSheet.create with no access to tokens and need factory conversion before any literal is reachable.

oracle.condition: Walk every .ts/.tsx file under app/ and src/components/, excluding app/_layout.tsx, src/components/UpdateCheckScreen.tsx and the Mapbox-native props in app/radar.tsx, matching numeric fontSize, fontWeight, borderRadius, padding*, gap, lineHeight and letterSpacing declarations.
oracle.assertion: The collected match array has length 0, down from the 901 measured on 2026-09-09.
oracle.failure_mode: Any file still carries an inline numeric style value, meaning that screen does not respond to a look change and renders Aurora proportions while set to Classic.

features.name: Each look offers only its own palettes
features.acceptance: When a unit test reads the palette set exposed for look aurora and for look classic, then aurora exposes exactly blaze plus timber while classic exposes exactly classic, dark, storm.
features.notes: This entry exists because holding look and palette fully independent broke once every Aurora candidate became dark. Pairing them is the fix; this test is what stops the pairing being silently undone.

oracle.condition: Call palettesForLook('aurora') and palettesForLook('classic') from src/theme/looks.ts.
oracle.assertion: palettesForLook('aurora') sorted deep-equals ['blaze','timber'] with length 2, and palettesForLook('classic') sorted deep-equals ['classic','dark','storm'] with length 3.
oracle.failure_mode: A palette is returned under the wrong look — blaze offered under classic — rendering a near-black ground against 12px radii and light-palette text colours.

features.name: Revert to Classic restores proportions and colours together
features.acceptance: When setLook('classic') is dispatched from a state where look equals aurora, then the resolved structural tokens and palette deep-equal the frozen Classic snapshot.
features.notes: The Classic snapshot must match src/theme/tokens.ts THEMES.classic byte-for-byte: background #F0F4F8, primary #1E3A5F, textPrimary #1A202C, freezeBlue #63B3ED. A partial revert leaves the user in a state neither look defines.

oracle.condition: Set useThemeStore state to { look: 'aurora', palette: 'timber' }, then call getState().setLook('classic').
oracle.assertion: getState().tokens deep-equals LOOKS.classic AND getState().palette equals 'classic' with getState().colors deep-equalling PALETTES.classic, whose values match src/theme/tokens.ts THEMES.classic byte-for-byte.
oracle.failure_mode: Structure reverts but colours stay dark, or colours revert but radii stay at 18 — a partial revert leaving a state neither look defines.

features.name: Look choice survives an app restart
features.acceptance: When the theme store rehydrates from AsyncStorage carrying a persisted look of classic, then the store resolves structural tokens to the classic set before first render.
features.notes: The existing store persists only themeName via partialize and re-resolves tokens in onRehydrateStorage. The look axis must follow the same pattern or a restart silently discards the user's choice. Persisted key is 'pingweather-theme' — unchanged, since renaming it would orphan every existing user's stored preference.

oracle.condition: Seed the AsyncStorage mock with key 'pingweather-theme' holding { state: { look: 'classic', palette: 'classic' } }, then trigger the store's onRehydrateStorage callback.
oracle.assertion: Immediately after rehydration and before any setLook call, getState().tokens deep-equals LOOKS.classic and getState().look equals 'classic'.
oracle.failure_mode: tokens remain LOOKS.aurora because onRehydrateStorage restored the look name without re-resolving the token object.

features.name: Mapbox native props survive the migration untouched
features.acceptance: When the migration has rewritten styling in app/radar.tsx, then the Mapbox-native RasterLayer style prop and styleURL constant are still present in Mapbox shape and the literal scanner is configured to skip them.
features.notes: The automated HALF of Scenario 6. Split from FEAT-007 deliberately: this proves the native prop SHAPE is preserved, which is a real falsifiable claim a unit test can own. It does NOT prove the map draws — that is FEAT-007 and only the operator can close it. Collapsing the two would let a unit test stand in as evidence for device rendering, which is exactly the laundering the contract forbids. FALSE-RED ON RECORD, 2026-09-11T04:17:44Z: chain record 6 says result=fail but this file was 6/6 GREEN in isolation at that moment. Cause — the file was written as pure regression guards, which protect already-correct state and therefore cannot go red before green; the recorded failure came from sibling suites in the same jest invocation, not from this test. Fixed by adding the 'radar.tsx consumes the token contract' assertion, which is false today (21 literals) and true only after TASK-009. Chain record 7 is the genuine RED, verified in isolation via --runTestsByPath. Record 6 is left in place because the chain is append-only and tamper-evident; deleting it would be the worse crime.

oracle.condition: Read app/radar.tsx from disk and assert on its source: the RasterLayer carries rasterOpacity, styleURL is a MapboxGL.StyleURL constant rather than a theme token, no MapboxGL element is assigned a React Native styles.* object, and setAccessToken remains above the default export.
oracle.assertion: All four source assertions hold, and __tests__/theme/noHardcodedLiterals.test.ts still contains the rasterOpacity|styleURL exclusion.
oracle.failure_mode: A migration rewrote MapboxGL.RasterLayer's style prop as an RN style object, or dropped the scanner exclusion so a later pass would rewrite it — the 2026-05-07 crash class.

features.name: Radar screen renders on a physical device
features.acceptance: When the operator opens the Radar screen in the EAS dev build on a physical Android device, then the Mapbox raster layer renders without crashing the screen.
features.notes: OPERATOR-ONLY. The bound test_file is FEAT-006's guard and is listed solely because every entry must be bound; it does NOT prove this claim and must never be cited as doing so. Nothing automated on this project can close this entry: the device tier has no runner, and __tests__/screens/radar.test.tsx mocks @rnmapbox/maps entirely at lines 28-44 so it cannot observe a native regression. To close, the operator must record device model, date, that map tiles drew, that the scrub control responded, and that no red-box appeared. Two broken OTAs shipped 2026-05-07 through exactly this gap.

oracle.condition: Install the EAS dev build carrying the migration, open the app, navigate to the Radar screen, and scrub the frame timeline.
oracle.assertion: The map tiles draw, the scrub control responds, and no red-box error or blank screen appears.
oracle.failure_mode: Blank screen or a native crash, indicating the migration rewrote MapboxGL.RasterLayer's style prop at app/radar.tsx line 65 as if it were a React Native style object.

features.name: Onboarding and legal screens render under both looks
features.acceptance: When the operator opens each of the 9 screens under app/onboarding/ and app/legal/ in the EAS dev build, under look aurora and then under look classic, then every screen renders with readable text and reachable controls in both.
features.source_scenario: AGENT-DERIVED: these 9 files are on the tdd-guard.yaml exclusion list and have no per-screen test of any kind, so nothing observes how they RENDER after the migration. FEAT-002's scan proves their literals are gone; no automated check on this project proves they still look right. The operator asked for EVERY screen to be upgraded, so leaving the only screens with zero UI coverage unowned would silently narrow that scope.
features.notes: OPERATOR-ONLY, and added by the orchestrator without being asked — the original write-up left this hole as a prose warning in tasks.md instead of giving it an owner, which is the failure mode this framework exists to remove. Scope: app/onboarding/{welcome,privacy,eula,battery-setup,location-setup,notification-setup,complete}.tsx and app/legal/{eula,privacy-policy}.tsx. The bound test_file is FEAT-002's scanner, listed because every entry must be bound; it proves the literals are gone, NOT that the screens render, and must never be cited as proof of the latter. To close, record device model, date, and a per-screen line for all 9 under BOTH looks. tdd-guard cannot be armed for these files: it matches by basename and no per-screen test exists, so removing the exclusion would block all work on them without adding any real coverage.

oracle.condition: Install the EAS dev build carrying the migration. Walk the onboarding wizard end to end and open both legal screens, first with look set to aurora, then repeat with look set to classic.
oracle.assertion: All 9 screens render with no clipped or overlapping text, every button and link is reachable and tappable, and no screen is blank or red-boxed — in both looks.
oracle.failure_mode: A screen renders with text clipped by a container sized for the other look's proportions, a control pushed off-screen, or a blank body where a factory conversion dropped the style object.
